learnings: Models need stronger guidance on distinguishing upstream application behavior from AUR injection. The threat model explicitly states that upstream behavior is not an injection, but models may still flag it if they see patterns like sending data to external services. The audit prompt should emphasize that files in the upstream source tree that are not executed during makepkg or installed as part of the package are out of scope.

File selection prioritization should deprioritize upstream infrastructure-as-code files (SST/Pulumi configs, cloud deployment configs) that are not executed during the AUR build process. Both models spent significant tokens reviewing files like infra/app.ts, infra/lake.ts, infra/secret.ts, which are deployment configs for the upstream project's cloud infrastructure and have no bearing on AUR package safety.

GitHub Actions workflow files (.github/workflows/* or similar) in the upstream source tree should be recognized as CI/CD tooling that does not execute during makepkg, unless the PKGBUILD explicitly references them. Models should not flag these as supply-chain risks unless the AUR maintainer modified them to inject malicious behavior.
